name.text: Relations Q8 - Restricting the domain of x squared

questiontext.text: The function f(x) = x2 for all real numbers does not have an inverse function because it is many-to-one. A teacher suggests restricting the domain to x greater than or equal to zero. Why does this restriction allow the function to have an inverse?

generalfeedback.text:
The original function f(x) = x2 is many-to-one because a positive number and its negative give the same square. For example, 3 and negative 3 both give 9.

An inverse function can only exist if the original relation is one-to-one, because the inverse must be able to send each output back to exactly one input.

By restricting the domain to x greater than or equal to zero, we remove all the negative inputs. Now every remaining input, being nonnegative, gives a different output from every other remaining input. The function has become one-to-one on this restricted domain, so an inverse function can now be defined. The correct answer is A.
